assertions.description: Document.prototype exposes the spellCheckCustomDictionary attribute (requires the SpellCheckCustomDictionaryAPI flag in Chrome 153).
The dictionary object exposes addWords as a function.
The dictionary object exposes removeWords as a function — essential for SPA view scoping and retracting mistakes.
The attribute is [SameObject]: repeated reads return the identical dictionary instance.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (!('spellCheckCustomDictionary' in Document.prototype)) return false; return document.spellCheckCustomDictionary === document.spellCheckCustomDictionary; })()

assertions.description: addWords and removeWords are undefined-returning fire-and-forget operations: a real add+remove round trip of a nonsense token completes without throwing and returns undefined from both calls.
assertions.test: (()=>{ const d = document.spellCheckCustomDictionary; if (!d || typeof d.addWords !== 'function') return false; try { const a = d.addWords(['zzqx-conf-token']); const r = d.removeWords(['zzqx-conf-token']); return a === undefined && r === undefined; } catch (e) { return false; } })()

assertions.description: The interface is deliberately write-only: no has/getWords/iteration surface may exist on the dictionary object (reading back would expose dictionary state). Holds on any engine that exposes the object.
assertions.test: (()=>{ const d = document.spellCheckCustomDictionary; if (!d) return false; return !('has' in d) && !('getWords' in d) && !(Symbol.iterator in d) && !('size' in d); })()

assertions.description: Adding a word suppresses its spell-check squiggle in editable fields for this document without touching the user's persistent dictionary (ignored-word semantics).
assertions.test: Requires visual observation with browser spell checking enabled: type an added word (e.g. Wolvic) in the editor demo's textarea before and after addWords and compare squiggles; then verify the word is still flagged in a different tab/site.
